findings.title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched away
findings.body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), which replaces the global `time.sleep`. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 (and `join()`'s internal sleeps) therefore return immediately and do not actually give the background flusher thread any time to produce. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is false, so the test still races `step.join()` (which sets `stopped=True`, causing the flusher loop to exit without flushing) against the flusher thread. This makes `test_basic` flaky: `(msg,) = messages` can fail with an empty list. The wait should use an un-patched sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep as real_sleep` or poll until `messages` is populated), not the patched `time.sleep`.

findings.title: Hung thread workers are never stopped and get duplicated on restart
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. In the `produce_to_pipe` code path (used by tests), workers are `threading.Thread` instances, so a thread flagged as hung (healthy_since exceeded `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds`) is never stopped. `_create_process_for_shards` is then called for the same shards, creating a second thread with a fresh `SpansBuffer`. Two flusher threads then concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same shards, producing duplicate segment messages and racing on segment acks. Thread mode should either be excluded from the health-restart logic or the old thread must be cooperatively stopped before spawning a replacement.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard but default is a single shared process
findings.body: The class docstring now says 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.' The implementation actually creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes and round-robins shards across them (`i % num_processes`). Moreover, the `--flusher-processes` click option defaults to 1, so with default configuration a single process handles all shards (the original behavior). The docstring misrepresents both the sharding scheme and the default; it should say that shards are distributed across up to `max_processes` flusher processes and that the default is one process for all shards.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name (`shard` vs `shards`) and misleading shard tag value
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 192) tag with `{"shard": shard_tag}`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (line 199) tags with `{"shards": shard_tag}`. `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of all shards handled by the process, not a single shard. The mismatched tag key means dashboards/alerts filtering on `shard` will silently miss `wait_produce`, and the singular `shard` tag now carries a multi-value string, breaking per-shard aggregation that previously keyed on a single (or absent) shard. Use one consistent tag key and document that its value is a shard list.

findings.title: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code
findings.body: The newly added `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` method (lines 127-132) is never called anywhere in the codebase; `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Leaving unused code adds maintenance burden and suggests a shard-level restart path that does not exist. It should be removed (or wired up) before merge.
